{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Democratic community policing would repudiate the excessive use of force by “proactive” police tactics and the use of SWAT teams.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Such policies would drastically reduce the chances of repeating the terror of Ferguson.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Mandated \"reverse surveillance\" technology such as dashboard and uniform cameras could reduce the willingness of police to engage in the excessive use of force.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A full, thorough Federal investigation into the events of August 9th is needed to provide justice to the family and friends of Michael Brown.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Such measures can only mitigate, not abolish, the effects of racist criminal justice policies and the absence of equality of opportunity for low-income Americans.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Actively challenging how law enforcement affects poor communities must be a priority for all working to build a better America.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Changes in criminal justice policies cannot by themselves bring justice to all Americans.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Social protest movements must demand government policies that serve the interests of all rather than those of a narrow elite.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Only by building a majoritarian movement for racial and economic justice can we reverse the growth of racial and class apartheid in the United States.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
